newsitem.title: CANADA: Black bear kills two in Canadian provincial park.
newsitem.headline: Black bear kills two in Canadian provincial park.

text.p: A black bear killed two people and injured two others in an attack in a Canadian provincial park in northern British Columbia on Friday, the Royal Canadian Mounted police said.

A 38-year old Texas woman and a 57-year old Canadian man from Fort Nelson were mauled and killed by the bear in the early morning attack at the Liard Hotsprings Park, about 200 miles (321.9 km) north of Fort Nelson on the Alaska Highway.

The woman's 13-year old son and a 20-year-old man from Calgary, Alberta were also hurt by the bear, but neither suffered life-threatening injuries, police said in a terse news release giving few details of the attack.
The 13-year-old boy was flown to British Columbia Children's Hospital in Vancouver and the injured man was being treated in an area hospital.
The Fort Nelson man was killed by the bear after rushing to help the woman and her son when the animal attacked them, an Environment Ministry spokeswoman said.
The bear was cornered and destroyed shortly after the incident.
Bear attacks on humans are extremely rare in Canadian wilderness areas, but it was the second time in recent months that people were mauled by bears in provincial parks.

Last month a young boy on a camping trip was dragged from his tent and badly injured by a hungry bear in Ontario's Algonquin Park in what park rangers described as a freak attack. The bear was driven off by a camp counselor, who smacked the animal with a canoe paddle.
It was the first bear attack in Algonquin Park since the early 1990s.

"In general, bear attacks are quite rare. There are an average of one person killed and five people injured in British Columbia a year by bears, both grizzlies and black bears," said Matt Austin of the wildlife branch of the province's Ministry of Environment, Lands and Parks.
